prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: genuinely transparent PNG sprite atlas of eight natural, irregular sheep flocks and cow herds for a painted European fantasy board-game map.
Composition: exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight separate groups, one group centered inside each cell, generous transparent gutters. Soft hand-painted gouache with natural anatomy, muted cream wool and earthy brown/black/white coats, gentle elevated three-quarter map view, upper-left light. Cohesive miniature illustrations, not cartoons or photographs.
Primary request: animal groups must look casually scattered while grazing, NOT arranged in a triangle, square, circle, neat row, parade or evenly spaced grid. Different individual body directions, asymmetrical outlines, uneven gaps, some close pairs and one animal farther away. Each group has a distinct shape, with no overlaps hiding bodies.
Top row, left to right: (1) two sheep, one side-on grazing left and the other standing diagonally right at a different depth, wide uneven gap; (2) three sheep in a loose crooked trail, mixed grazing and alert poses, one distinctly off to the side; (3) five cream sheep scattered in an asymmetrical wide patch, two nearby and three farther apart, one lying down; (4) four sheep, one dark sheep, a loose lopsided group with a detached straggler, all facing different directions.
Bottom row: (5) two cows in opposite orientations, one grazing and one looking outward, separated asymmetrically; (6) three brown-white cows in an uneven elongated diagonal, one lying down, varied angles; (7) four cows in an irregular broad scattering, one black-white and varied chestnut coats, open empty space inside group and unequal distances; (8) five mixed cream/brown cows, small loose cluster of three plus two detached grazers, several different orientations and postures.
Keep each animal distinct and legible when a whole group is rendered only 26–40 pixels wide on a map. Do not enlarge heads or eyes. No scenery, grass or ground patches, buildings, people, fences, shadows filling background, text, labels or grid lines. Genuine transparent alpha throughout every empty space, NOT a painted checkerboard. Keep all animals fully inside their respective atlas cells. Do not reuse a repeated uniform arrangement across groups.
